claims.text: The MgAlCuZnGd high-entropy alloy has a density below 6 g/cm³.
The as-cast MgAlCuZnGd alloy is a metastable single-phase solid solution.
The as-cast alloy contains minimal pre-existing metastable intermetallic precursors.
Thermal aging at 500°C causes Mg to diffuse from the metastable matrix toward grain boundaries.
Mg redistribution during aging nucleates fine Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
Mg-rich precipitates form both along grain boundaries and at intragranular sites.
The extent and size of Mg-rich precipitation increase with aging duration.
Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates create localized electrochemical inhomogeneities that act as galvanic cells.
Precipitate-induced galvanic cells increase localized corrosion relative to the as-cast alloy.
Localized corrosion rate is directly correlated with the extent of Mg-rich precipitation.
Mg-rich precipitates interfere with uniform oxide-scale formation during high-temperature oxidation.
Aged alloys form thicker and less protective oxide scales than the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast homogeneous alloy exhibits low localized corrosion.
The as-cast alloy forms a uniform, protective oxide scale under high-temperature conditions.
The controlled comparison uses as-cast specimens and specimens aged at 500°C in high-purity Ar for 5, 10, and 20 hours.
Corrosion is evaluated in 3.5% NaCl, and oxidation is evaluated in air at 600–700°C.
Failure to detect Mg segregation and Mg-rich precipitates, or statistically significant corrosion and oxidation changes relative to the as-cast control, would falsify the hypothesis.
